title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第七十五: 張鎰 劉從一 蕭復 柳渾
title.en: Volume 125 Biographies 75: Zhang Yi, Liu Congyi, Xiao Fu, Liu Hun
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 列傳第七十五: 張鎰 劉從一 蕭復 柳渾 Volume 125 Biographies 75: Zhang Yi, Liu Congyi, Xiao Fu, Liu Hun

sentences.zh: 張鎰，蘇州人，朔方節度使齊丘之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was a native of Suzhou, the son of Qiqiu, military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, a native of Suzhou, was the son of Qiqiu, the Shuofang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以門廕授左衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed Left Guard Army Cao staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he was appointed staff officer in the Left Guard Army bureau.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀為關內副元帥，以嘗伏事齊丘，辟鎰為判官。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi served as deputy commander of Guannei, because he had once served Qiqiu in subordination, he recruited Yi as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi was deputy commander-in-chief for the interior passes, having once served under Qiqiu, he brought Yi on as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and then promoted to palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，華原令盧樅以公事呵責邑人內侍齊令詵，令詵銜之，構誣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, Lu Cong, magistrate of Huayuan, publicly rebuked the local man and eunuch Qi Lingshen on official business; Lingshen bore a grudge and fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianyuan, Lu Cong, the Huayuan magistrate, had rebuked the local eunuch Qi Lingshen on official business; Lingshen nursed a grievance and trumped up accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 外發鎰按驗，樅當降官，及下有司，樅當杖死。

translations.literal: Yi was sent out to investigate; Cong should have been demoted in rank, but once the case reached the responsible offices, Cong faced death by beating.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to Yi for investigation; Cong was due to be reduced in rank, but once it reached the judicial offices he was slated for death by flogging.

sentences.zh: 鎰其公服白其母曰：「上疏理樅，樅必免死，鎰必坐貶。

translations.literal: Yi, still in his official robes, told his mother: "If I memorialize to vindicate Cong, Cong will surely escape death, but Yi will surely be punished with demotion."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing his court robes, Yi spoke to his mother: "If I submit a memorial to clear Cong, he will certainly be spared, but I will certainly be demoted."

sentences.zh: 若以私則鎰負於當官，貶則以太夫人為憂，敢問所安？

translations.literal: If I act from private feeling then I fail in my duty as an official; if demoted, my greatest worry is for the Lady Dowager — where is your peace of mind?
translations.idiomatic: "If I favor him out of personal loyalty I betray my public duty; if I am demoted, it is my mother I fear for most — which course do you prefer?"

sentences.zh: 」母曰：爾無累於道，吾所安也。

translations.literal: Mother said: You will not compromise the Way — that is my peace.
translations.idiomatic: His mother replied: "You will not stain your integrity — that is comfort enough for me."

sentences.zh: 」遂執奏正罪，樅獲配流，鎰貶撫州司戶。

translations.literal: He then resolutely memorialized to establish the proper punishment; Cong was sentenced to exile, and Yi was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He duly memorialized to fix the sentence; Cong was banished, and Yi was demoted to registrar at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 量移晉陵令，未之官，洪吉觀察張鎬辟為判官，奏授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Jinling but did not take up the post; Zhang Hao, observer of Hongji, recruited him as administrative aide and memorialized to appoint him palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Jinling but never took office; Zhang Hao, the Hongji observer, brought him on as chief clerk and had him appointed palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 遷屯田員外郎，轉祠部、右司二員外。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture and transferred to vice director posts in the Ministries of Rites and of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then served as vice director in both the Ministry of Rites and the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母憂居喪有聞，免喪，除司勛員外。

translations.literal: His mourning for his mother won renown; after the mourning period ended he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for the way he observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning ended he was made vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 交遊不雜，與楊綰、崔祐甫相善。

translations.literal: His social circle was not mixed; he was on good terms with Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his company select and was close to Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，除濠州刺史，為政清凈，州事大理。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was appointed prefect of Hao; his governance was pure and quiet, and prefectural affairs were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 5 he was made prefect of Hao; his administration was clean and restrained, and the prefecture was brought thoroughly to order.

sentences.zh: 乃招經術之士，講訓生徒，比去郡，升明經者四十余人。

translations.literal: He then recruited scholars of the classics to lecture and instruct students; by the time he left the prefecture, more than forty had passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited classical scholars to lecture his students, and by the time he left the prefecture more than forty had passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 撰《三禮圖》九卷、《五經微旨》十四卷、《孟子音義》三卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Illustrations of the Three Rites in nine juan, Subtle Purport of the Five Classics in fourteen juan, and Phonetic Glosses on Mencius in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Illustrations of the Three Rites in nine fascicles, Subtle Purport of the Five Classics in fourteen fascicles, and Phonetic Glosses on Mencius in three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜反於汴州，鎰訓練鄉兵，嚴守禦之備，詔書褒異，加侍御史、沿淮鎮守使。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Yi trained local militia and strictly prepared defenses; an imperial edict praised him exceptionally and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner guarding the Huai frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Yi drilled local militia and tightened the defenses; an edict singled him out for praise and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner guarding the Huai frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋遷壽州刺史，使如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be prefect of Shou, his commissioner duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Shou while retaining his commissioner duties.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，除江南西道都團練觀察使、洪州刺史、兼御史中丞，征拜吏部侍郎，尋除河中晉絳都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, Yi was appointed overall training-and-observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit, prefect of Hong, and concurrently vice censor-in-chief; he was summoned as vice minister of Personnel, then soon made defense-and-observation commissioner of Hezhong Jin- and Jiang-prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong acceded, Yi was made overall training-and-observation commissioner for Jiangnan West, prefect of Hong, and concurrent vice censor-in-chief; he was then summoned as vice minister of Personnel and soon appointed defense-and-observation commissioner for Hezhong and the Jin and Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 到官數日，改汴滑節度觀察使、汴州刺史、兼御史大夫，以疾辭，逗留於中路，征入，養疾私第。

translations.literal: Within days of reaching his post he was changed to Bian-Slip military commissioner, prefect of Bian, and concurrent censor-in-chief; he declined on grounds of illness, lingered on the road, was recalled, and convalesced at his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Only days after taking office he was reassigned as Bian-Slip military commissioner, prefect of Bian, and concurrent censor-in-chief; pleading illness he stalled on the road, was recalled, and recuperated at home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿學士，修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 建中三年正月，太仆卿趙縱為奴當千發其陰事，縱下御史臺，貶循州司馬，留當千於內侍省。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, Minister of Imperial Studs Zhao Zong was exposed for private misconduct by his slave Dangqian; Zong was sent to the Censorate, demoted to military adjutant of Xunzhou, and Dangqian was detained in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianzhong 3, Minister of Imperial Studs Zhao Zong was denounced for private misconduct by his slave Dangqian; Zong was handed to the Censorate and demoted to military adjutant of Xunzhou, while Dangqian was kept in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 鎰上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial on the matter, writing:

sentences.zh: 伏見趙縱為奴所告下獄，人皆震懼，未測聖情。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that Zhao Zong was imprisoned on a slave's accusation; everyone is shaken with fear and cannot fathom Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Zhao Zong has been imprisoned on a slave's accusation; the court is shaken with fear and cannot read Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，太宗謂侍臣曰：比有奴告其主謀逆，此極弊法，特須禁斷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan the Taizong Emperor told his attendants: Recently slaves have accused their masters of plotting rebellion — this is an extremely harmful practice and must be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 Emperor Taizong told his attendants: "Of late slaves have been accusing their masters of treason — this is a ruinous practice and must be stopped outright."

sentences.zh: 假令有謀反者，必不獨成，自有他人論之，豈藉其奴告也。

translations.literal: Even if there were a plotter, he could not accomplish it alone; others would certainly report it — why rely on a slave's accusation?
translations.idiomatic: Even if someone were plotting rebellion, he could not act alone; others would report it — why depend on a slave's word?

sentences.zh: 自今已後，奴告主者皆不受，盡令斬決。

translations.literal: From now on, any slave who accuses his master shall not be accepted — all such accusers shall be executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth no accusation by a slave against his master shall be accepted; every such accuser shall be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」由是賤不得幹貴，下不得陵上，教化之本既正，悖亂之漸不生。

translations.literal: Thus the base could not interfere with the noble, nor the low overbear the high; the root of moral transformation was set right, and the seeds of disorder did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the low could not meddle with the high, nor the base overbear the noble; the foundation of moral order was secured and the seeds of disorder did not take root.

sentences.zh: 為國之經，百代難改，欲全其事體，實在防微。

translations.literal: As a constant of statecraft, it is hard to alter for a hundred generations; to preserve the integrity of the institution, one must truly guard against the slightest breach.
translations.idiomatic: As a constant of statecraft it is not lightly changed across generations; to preserve its integrity one must guard against the smallest breach.

sentences.zh: 頃者長安令李濟得罪因奴，萬年令霍晏得罪因婢，愚賤之輩，悖慢成風，主反畏之，動遭誣告，充溢府縣，莫能斷決。

translations.literal: Recently Chang'an magistrate Li Ji was punished because of a slave, and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan because of a maid; among the foolish and base, insolence became the fashion, masters came to fear them, and false accusations multiplied until the prefectures and counties were overwhelmed and could not decide cases.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Chang'an magistrate Li Ji and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan were ruined by slaves and maids respectively; among servants insolence became epidemic, masters lived in fear of them, and false accusations flooded the prefectures until courts could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 建中元年五月二十八日，詔曰：準鬥競律，諸奴婢告主，非謀叛已上者，同自首法，並準律處分。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month of the first year of Jianzhong an edict said: According to the statute on brawling, whenever slaves or maids accuse their masters of offenses short of plotting rebellion, they are treated like voluntary confessors and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month of Jianzhong 1 an edict declared: "Under the brawling statute, any slave or maid who accuses a master of a crime short of treason is treated as a voluntary confessor and punished under the code."

sentences.zh: 」自此奴婢復順，獄訴稍息。

translations.literal: From then on slaves and maids again became obedient, and prison suits gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After that servants again kept their place, and lawsuits from the prisons gradually quieted.

sentences.zh: 今趙縱非叛逆，奴實奸兇，奴在禁中，縱獨下獄，考之於法，或恐未正。

translations.literal: Now Zhao Zong is not a rebel; the slave is truly treacherous and vicious — the slave is detained in the palace quarters while Zong alone is imprisoned; examined against the law, this may perhaps not be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zong is no rebel; the slave is the guilty party, yet the slave remains in palace custody while Zong alone sits in prison — judged by the code, this may not be just.

sentences.zh: 將帥之功，莫大於子儀；

translations.literal: Among generals' achievements, none is greater than Guo Ziyi's;
translations.idiomatic: No general's service has surpassed Guo Ziyi's;

sentences.zh: 人臣之位，莫大於尚父。

translations.literal: among subjects' ranks, none is higher than the Sublime Father's.
translations.idiomatic: and no subject ever stood higher than the Sublime Father.

sentences.zh: 歿身未幾，墳土僅乾，兩婿先已當辜，趙縱今又下獄。

translations.literal: Hardly had his body been buried and the grave earth barely dry when two sons-in-law were already punished, and now Zhao Zong is again imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he been buried when the grave was still fresh, yet two sons-in-law had already been punished and now Zhao Zong is imprisoned again.

sentences.zh: 設令縱實抵法，所告非奴，才經數月，連罪三婿。

translations.literal: Even if Zong truly violated the law, the accuser was not a slave — in only a few months three sons-in-law have been punished in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zong were truly guilty, the accuser was not a slave — within a few months three sons-in-law have been punished in succession.

sentences.zh: 錄勛念舊，猶或可容，況在章程，本宜宥免。

translations.literal: Recording merit and remembering old service, he might still be tolerated; moreover under the statutes he ought originally to have been pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for his father's merit he might still be spared; under the statutes he ought in any case to be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 陛下方誅群賊，大用武臣，雖見寵於當時，恐息望於他日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now suppressing the rebel hosts and greatly employing military men; though they enjoy favor at present, they may lose hope for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is crushing the rebels and relying heavily on military men; though favored now, they may lose heart for the days ahead.

sentences.zh: 太宗之令典尚在，陛下之明詔始行，一朝偕違，不與眾守，於教化恐失，於刑法恐煩，所益悉無，所傷至廣。

translations.literal: Taizong's exemplary decree still stands, and Your Majesty's clear edict has only just been promulgated — to violate both at once and not abide with the multitude in observance may lose moral transformation and burden the penal code; the gain is nothing, the harm very wide.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's exemplary decree still stands and Your Majesty's own edict has only just been issued — to break both at once and not hold the court to them risks moral order and clutters the penal code; nothing is gained and the harm is great.

sentences.zh: 臣非私趙縱，非惡此奴，叨居股肱，職在匡弼，斯昌大體，敢不極言。

translations.literal: Your servant does not favor Zhao Zong privately nor hate this slave; holding a post among Your Majesty's closest limbs, my duty is to assist and correct — on so great a matter how dare I not speak to the utmost?
translations.idiomatic: I do not plead for Zhao Zong out of private interest nor out of hatred for this slave; as one of Your Majesty's closest advisers it is my duty to speak plainly on matters of state, and on so grave a point I dare not hold back.

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖慈，納臣愚懇。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your sacred compassion to accept your servant's earnest plea.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to accept this earnest plea.

sentences.zh: 上深納之，縱於是左貶而已，當千杖殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it; Zong was merely demoted to a lower post, and Dangqian was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the advice to heart; Zong was merely demoted, and Dangqian was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 鎰乃令召子儀家僮數百人，以死奴示之。

translations.literal: Yi then ordered several hundred of Guo Ziyi's household slaves summoned and showed them the dead slave.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then had several hundred of Guo Ziyi's household slaves summoned and showed them the executed slave.

sentences.zh: 盧杞忌鎰名重道直，無以陷之，以方用兵西邊，杞乃偽請行，上固以不可，因薦鎰以中書侍郎為鳳翔隴右節度使代硃泚，與吐蕃相尚結贊等盟於清水。

translations.literal: Lu Qi resented Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to trap him; as troops were being used on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person; the emperor firmly refused, and therefore recommended Yi, as vice director of the Secretariat, to be Fengxiang-Longyou military commissioner in place of Zhu Ci, to ally at Qingshui with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi resented Yi's reputation and integrity and could find no way to ruin him; with war underway in the west Qi pretended to offer to go himself, the emperor refused, and Qi instead recommended Yi — still vice director of the Secretariat — as Fengxiang-Longyou military commissioner replacing Zhu Ci, to treat with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 將盟，鎰與結贊約各以二千人赴壇所，執兵者半之，列於壇外二百步；

translations.literal: Before the alliance, Yi and Jiezan agreed that each would bring two thousand men to the altar site; half of them armed, arrayed two hundred paces outside the altar;
translations.idiomatic: Before the rites Yi and Jiezan agreed that each side would bring two thousand men to the altar; half would bear arms, stationed two hundred paces from the altar;

sentences.zh: 散從者半之，分立壇下。

translations.literal: half the attendants unarmed, standing separately below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: and half would be unarmed attendants posted below the altar.

sentences.zh: 鎰與賓佐齊映、齊抗及盟官崔漢衡、樊澤、常魯、於頔等七人，皆朝服；

translations.literal: Yi with his aides Qi Ying and Qi Kang and alliance officers Cui Hanheng, Fan Ze, Chang Lu, Yu Zhen, and others — seven in all — all in court dress;
translations.idiomatic: Yi, his aides Qi Ying and Qi Kang, and the treaty officers Cui Hanheng, Fan Ze, Chang Lu, and Yu Zhen — seven in all — all wore court dress;

sentences.zh: 結贊與其本國將相論悉頰藏、論臧熱、論利陁、斯官者、論力徐等亦七人，俱升壇為盟。

translations.literal: Jiezan with his own country's generals and ministers Lun Xijianzang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Siguanzhe, Lun Lixu, and others — also seven — all ascended the altar to conclude the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan with his own generals and ministers Lun Xijianzang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Siguanzhe, and Lun Lixu — also seven — all ascended the altar to swear the treaty.

sentences.zh: 初，約漢以牛，蕃以馬為牲，鎰恥與之盟，將殺其禮，乃請結贊曰：「漢非牛不田，蕃非馬不行，今請以羊豕犬三物代之。

translations.literal: At first it was agreed that the Han would use an ox and the Tibetans a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally on those terms and wished to diminish the ceremony, so he asked Jiezan: "The Han cannot farm without oxen, nor the Tibetans travel without horses — now let us substitute sheep, swine, and dogs."
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Han were to sacrifice an ox and the Tibetans a horse; Yi found the parity demeaning and sought to scale back the rite, telling Jiezan: "The Han cannot farm without oxen nor Tibetans travel without horses — let us substitute sheep, swine, and dogs instead."

sentences.zh: 」結贊許諾。

translations.literal: Jiezan consented.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan agreed.

sentences.zh: 時塞外無豕，結贊請以羝羊，鎰出犬、白羊，乃坎於壇北刑之，雜血一器而歃，盟文曰：

translations.literal: At that time there were no swine beyond the frontier; Jiezan asked to use a ram instead, Yi produced a dog and a white sheep; they then cut a pit north of the altar and slaughtered them there, mixed the blood in one vessel and drank it, and the alliance text read:
translations.idiomatic: Swine were unavailable beyond the frontier, so Jiezan offered a ram while Yi provided a dog and a white sheep; they cut a pit north of the altar, slaughtered the animals there, mixed the blood in one bowl and drank it, and the treaty text read:

sentences.zh: 唐有天下，恢奄禹跡，舟車所至，莫不率俾。

translations.literal: Tang possesses the realm, broadly covering the traces of Yu; wherever carriage and boat can reach, none fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Tang holds the realm, spanning the domain Yu once traced; wherever cart and boat can reach, all submit.

sentences.zh: 以累聖重光，卜年惟永，恢王者之丕業，被四海以聲教。

translations.literal: Through successive sage emperors the radiance is renewed, the years divined for endless duration, the kingly great enterprise restored, and the four seas clothed in civilizing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive sage rulers the dynasty shines anew, its years foretold as endless, its royal enterprise restored, and the four seas clothed in civilizing instruction.

sentences.zh: 與吐蕃贊普，代為婚姻，因結鄰好，安危同體，甥舅之國，將二百年。

translations.literal: With the Tibetan tsenpo, generation after generation we have been joined in marriage, thereby forming neighborly friendship, sharing safety and danger as one body — a nephew-and-uncle state for nearly two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: With the Tibetan emperor we have been linked by marriage for generations, bound as neighbors who share fortune and peril — a nephew-and-uncle relationship for nearly two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 其間或因小忿，棄惠為仇，封疆騷然，靡有寧歲。

translations.literal: In the interval, at times over small resentments we cast aside kindness for enmity; the borders were disturbed and there were no peaceful years.
translations.idiomatic: At times small grievances turned kindness to enmity; the frontiers were troubled and peace was rare.

sentences.zh: 皇帝踐阼，湣茲黎元，乃釋俘囚悉歸蕃落。

translations.literal: The emperor has ascended the throne, pitying the black-haired people, and therefore released captives to return them all to Tibetan settlements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has taken the throne, pitying the people, and released captives to return them all to Tibetan lands.

sentences.zh: 二國展禮，同茲協和，行人往復，累布成命。

translations.literal: The two states have extended ritual courtesies, sharing this harmony; envoys have gone back and forth, repeatedly promulgating settled orders.
translations.idiomatic: Both courts have exchanged ritual courtesies in this spirit of harmony; envoys have shuttled back and forth bearing settled agreements.

sentences.zh: 是必詐謀不起，兵革不用矣。

translations.literal: Thus treacherous designs surely will not arise, and arms need not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Thus treachery shall not arise and arms need not be taken up.

sentences.zh: 彼猶以兩國之要，求之永久，古有結盟，今請用之。

translations.literal: They still regard the essentials of the two states as seeking permanence; alliance existed in antiquity — now we request to employ it.
translations.idiomatic: They still hold that the vital interests of both states call for permanence; alliances were made in antiquity — let that practice serve now.

sentences.zh: 國家務息邊人，外其故地，棄利蹈義，堅盟從約。

translations.literal: The state is intent on giving rest to the frontier people, setting aside former territories, abandoning profit to follow righteousness, and firmly allying in observance of the pact.
translations.idiomatic: The court seeks peace for the frontier peoples, yields former territories, forsakes profit for righteousness, and binds itself firmly to the treaty.

sentences.zh: 今國家所守界：涇州西至彈箏峽西口，隴州西至清水縣，鳳州西至同谷縣，暨劍南西山、大渡河東，為漢界。

translations.literal: The boundaries the state now holds: from Jingzhou west to the western mouth of Tanqi Gorge, from Longzhou west to Qingshui County, from Fengzhou west to Tonggu County, and including the western mountains of Jiannan and east of the Dadu River — this is the Han frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Han frontier now held runs from Jingzhou west to the western mouth of Tanqi Gorge, from Longzhou west to Qingshui County, from Fengzhou west to Tonggu County, and includes the western mountains of Jiannan and the lands east of the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 蕃國守鎮在蘭、渭、原、會，西至臨洮，又東至成州，抵劍南西界磨些諸蠻、大渡水西南，為蕃界。

translations.literal: The Tibetan state's garrison posts are at Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, west to Lintao, and east again to Chengzhou, reaching the Mosuo tribes and other barbarians on the western border of Jiannan and southwest of the Dadu River — this is the Tibetan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan frontier runs through garrisons at Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, west to Lintao and east to Chengzhou, reaching the Mosuo and other tribes on Jiannan's western marches and southwest of the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 其兵馬鎮守之處州縣見有居人，彼此兩邊見屬漢諸蠻，以今所分見住處依前所有不載者，蕃有兵馬處蕃守，漢有兵馬處漢守，不得侵越。

translations.literal: Where troops are stationed in prefectures and counties that have inhabitants, and on both sides among the various tribes subject to the Han, according to the present division of where people now dwell, retaining prior holdings not recorded — where Tibet has troops Tibet shall guard, where Han has troops Han shall guard, and neither may encroach.
translations.idiomatic: In prefectures and counties where troops are posted and people dwell, and among the tribal peoples on either side now assigned to each realm according to present residence and prior holdings not listed here — where Tibet posts troops Tibet shall guard, where Han posts troops Han shall guard, and neither may encroach.

sentences.zh: 其先未有兵馬處，不得雜置並築城堡耕種。

translations.literal: In places that previously had no troops, mixed garrisons may not be placed, nor fortresses built and fields cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: In areas that previously had no troops, neither side may establish mixed garrisons, build fortresses, or open fields.

sentences.zh: 今二國將相受辭而會，齋戒將事，告天地山川之神，惟神昭臨，無得衍墜。

translations.literal: Now the generals and ministers of the two states, having received the text, meet, fast and purify themselves for the rite, and announce it to the spirits of Heaven, Earth, mountains, and rivers — may the spirits clearly witness and let none fall short or exceed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the generals and ministers of both states, having received the text, meet in ritual purity and announce it to the spirits of heaven, earth, mountains, and rivers — may they witness clearly, and let none fall short or exceed.

sentences.zh: 其盟文藏於郊廟，副在有司，二國之誠，其永保之。

translations.literal: The alliance text shall be stored in the suburban and ancestral temples, with a copy held by the responsible offices; the sincerity of the two states — may it be forever preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty text shall be deposited in the suburban and ancestral temples, with a copy held by the responsible offices; may the sincerity of both states be preserved forever.

sentences.zh: 結贊亦出盟文，不加於坎，但埋牲而已。

translations.literal: Jiezan also produced an alliance text, not adding it to the pit but only burying the victims.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan also produced a treaty text, which was not placed in the pit but only buried with the sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 盟畢，結贊請鎰就壇之西南隅佛幄中焚香為誓，誓畢，復升壇飲酒。

translations.literal: When the alliance was concluded, Jiezan asked Yi to go to the Buddhist canopy at the altar's southwest corner to burn incense in oath; when the oath was finished they again ascended the altar to drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, Jiezan asked Yi to burn incense in oath at the Buddhist canopy on the altar's southwest corner; after the oath they again ascended the altar to drink wine.

sentences.zh: 獻酬之禮，各用其物，以將厚意而歸。

translations.literal: In the rites of offering and return, each used his own goods to convey deep regard on departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the exchange of gifts each side used its own goods to convey goodwill on parting.

sentences.zh: 德宗將幸奉天，鎰竊知之，將迎鑾駕，具財貨服用獻行在。

translations.literal: Dezong was about to proceed to Fengtian; Yi learned of it in secret and prepared to welcome the imperial carriage, assembling wealth, goods, and clothing to present at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was about to flee to Fengtian, Yi learned of it in advance and prepared to welcome the imperial train, assembling supplies and clothing to present at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 李楚琳者，嘗事硃泚，得其心。

translations.literal: Li Chulin had once served Zhu Ci and won his confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chulin had once served under Zhu Ci and won his trust.

sentences.zh: 軍司馬齊映等密謀曰：「楚琳不去，必為亂。

translations.literal: Army marshal Qi Ying and others secretly plotted, saying: "If Chulin is not removed, he will surely cause disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Army marshal Qi Ying and others plotted in secret: "If Chulin is not sent away, he will surely rebel."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣楚琳屯於隴州。

translations.literal: They then dispatched Chulin to garrison Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Chulin to garrison Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 楚琳知其謀，乃托故不時發。

translations.literal: Chulin knew their plot and therefore pleaded some excuse not to depart on time.
translations.idiomatic: Chulin saw through the plot and stalled his departure on one pretext after another.

sentences.zh: 鎰始以迎駕心憂惑，以楚琳承命去矣，殊不促其行。

translations.literal: Yi at first, preoccupied with welcoming the emperor, thought Chulin had already accepted orders to leave and did not at all press him to march.
translations.idiomatic: Preoccupied with welcoming the emperor, Yi assumed Chulin had already accepted orders to leave and did not press him to march.

sentences.zh: 鎰修飾邊幅，不為軍士所悅。

translations.literal: Yi was fastidious in dress and deportment and was not liked by the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was fastidious in dress and manner and was not liked by the troops.

sentences.zh: 是夜，楚琳遂與其黨王汾、李卓、牛僧伽等作亂。

translations.literal: That night Chulin then rose in revolt with his partisans Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chulin rebelled with his partisans Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others.

sentences.zh: 鎰夜縋而走，判官齊映自水竇出，齊抗為傭保負荷而逃，皆獲免。

translations.literal: Yi was let down by rope at night and fled; administrative aide Qi Ying escaped through a water conduit, and Qi Kang was carried off by a porter — all escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was lowered by rope at night and fled; Qi Ying escaped through a water conduit and Qi Kang was carried off by a porter — all escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 鎰出鳳翔三十里，及二子皆為候騎所得，楚琳俱殺之；

translations.literal: Thirty li outside Fengxiang Yi and his two sons were all seized by scouting horsemen, and Chulin killed them all;
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li outside Fengxiang Yi and his two sons were seized by scouting horsemen and Chulin had them all killed;

sentences.zh: 判官王沼、張元度、柳遇、李漵被殺。

translations.literal: administrative aides Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin were killed.
translations.idiomatic: and the aides Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 尋贈太子太傅，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with funeral expenses supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with state-provided funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 馮河清者，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Feng Heqing was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Heqing was a native of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 初以武藝從軍，隸朔方節度郭子儀，以戰功授左衛大將軍同正；

translations.literal: At first he entered the army through martial skill, served under Shuofang commissioner Guo Ziyi, and was appointed Left Guard grand general with concurrent status for military merit;
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service through martial skill under Shuofang commissioner Guo Ziyi and was made Left Guard grand general with concurrent status for distinguished combat;

sentences.zh: 隸涇原節度馬璘，頻以偏師禦吐蕃，甚有殺獲之功。

translations.literal: he then served under Jingyuan commissioner Ma Lin, frequently leading detached columns against the Tibetans with great success in killing and capturing.
translations.idiomatic: then served under Jingyuan commissioner Ma Lin, repeatedly leading detached columns against Tibet with notable kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 歷試太子詹事、兼御史中丞，充兵馬使。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，節度使姚令言奉詔率兵赴關東，以河清知兵馬留後，判官、殿中侍御史姚況知州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, military commissioner Yao Lingyan was ordered to lead troops east to the passes; Heqing was made acting military rear commander, and administrative aide and palace censor Yao Kuang managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4 commissioner Yao Lingyan was ordered east with his troops; Heqing was left as acting rear commander while aide and palace censor Yao Kuang ran prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 及令言至京師，所統兵叛，上幸奉天，河清與況聞之，乃集三軍大哭，因共激勵將吏，誓敦誠節，眾頗義之。

translations.literal: When Lingyan reached the capital his troops mutinied and the emperor proceeded to Fengtian; Heqing and Kuang, on hearing it, assembled the three armies and wept aloud, then together roused officers and clerks to pledge sincere loyalty — the host was much moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingyan reached the capital his troops mutinied and the emperor fled to Fengtian; Heqing and Kuang assembled the army, wept aloud, and together rallied the officers to pledge loyalty — the troops were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 即時發甲仗、器械、車百余輛，連夜送行在所。

translations.literal: They immediately dispatched armor, weapons, equipment, and more than a hundred carts, sending them overnight to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately dispatched armor, weapons, equipment, and more than a hundred carts to the traveling court that same night.

sentences.zh: 時駕初遷幸，六軍雖集，蒼黃之際，都無戎器，及涇州甲仗至，軍士大振，特詔褒其誠效，拜四鎮北庭行軍涇原節度使、兼御史大夫；

translations.literal: The imperial train had just relocated; though the six armies were gathered, in the sudden crisis there were no weapons at all — when Jingzhou armor arrived the soldiers were greatly heartened; a special edict praised their loyal service and appointed Heqing Four Garrisons Beiting campaign Jingyuan military commissioner and concurrent censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: The court had just fled in disarray; though the six armies were gathered, they had no arms — when Jingzhou's armor arrived the troops were heartened; a special edict praised their loyalty and made Heqing Four Garrisons Beiting campaign Jingyuan military commissioner and concurrent censor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 姚況兼御史中丞、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Yao Kuang was made concurrent vice censor-in-chief and campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Kuang was made concurrent vice censor-in-chief and campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 俄加河清檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon Heqing was additionally made acting minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Heqing was soon additionally made acting minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 賊泚及姚令言累遣間諜招誘，河清輒拘而戮焉。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan repeatedly sent spies to entice him; Heqing always seized and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan repeatedly sent agents to win him over; Heqing always seized and executed them.

sentences.zh: 及駕幸梁州，其將田希鑒潛通泚，使結兇黨害河清。

translations.literal: When the emperor proceeded to Liangzhou, his general Tian Xijian secretly communicated with Ci and had vicious partisans kill Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Liangzhou, his general Tian Xijian secretly contacted Zhu Ci and had accomplices murder Heqing.

sentences.zh: 尋贈尚書左僕射，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with funeral expenses supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with state-provided funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he was posthumously appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan 1 he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉從一，中書侍郎林甫之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Congyi was the great-great-grandson of Vice Director of the Secretariat Lin Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi was the great-great-grandson of Vice Director Lin Fu.

sentences.zh: 祖令植，禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingzhi was Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingzhi had been Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父孺之，京兆府少尹。

translations.literal: His father Ruzhi was Junior Assistant Governor of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ruzhi had been junior assistant governor of the Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從一少舉進士，大歷中宏詞，授秘書省校書郎，以調中第，補渭南尉，雅為常袞所推重。

translations.literal: Congyi in youth passed the jinshi examination; in the Dali era he passed the hongci and was appointed collator in the Secretariat; through the transfer examination he ranked in the middle tier and was made magistrate of Weinan — he was greatly esteemed by Chang Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi passed the jinshi examination in his youth, then the hongci in the Dali era and was appointed a Secretariat collator; ranked in the middle tier of the transfer examination, he became magistrate of Weinan and was highly regarded by Chang Gun.

sentences.zh: 及袞為相，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: When Gun became chief minister, Congyi was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gun became chief minister, Congyi was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 居無何，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，宰相盧杞薦之，超遷侍御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, chief minister Lu Qi recommended him and he was promoted over the usual steps to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, chief minister Lu Qi recommended him and he was promoted directly to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 居數月，以親避除刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: After several months, on grounds of kinship avoidance he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was made vice director in the Ministry of Justice under kinship-avoidance rules.

sentences.zh: 建中末，普王之為元帥也，遷吏部郎中、兼御史中丞，為元帥判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong, when the Prince of Pu was made commander-in-chief, Congyi was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, serving as the commander's administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianzhong, when the Prince of Pu was made commander-in-chief, Congyi became director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, serving as the prince's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，拜刑部侍郎、平章事，從幸梁州。

translations.literal: While Dezong was at Fengtian, Congyi was appointed vice minister of Justice and Grand Councilor, accompanying the emperor to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezong was at Fengtian, Congyi was made vice minister of Justice and Grand Councilor and accompanied the emperor to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，改中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he was changed to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year he was reassigned as vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 歲中，加集賢殿大學士、修史。

translations.literal: Within the year he was additionally made senior academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and compiler of history.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was additionally made senior academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and charged with compiling history.

sentences.zh: 上遇之甚厚，以容身遠罪而已，不能有所匡輔。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him very generously, but he sought only to preserve himself and keep clear of blame and could not offer corrective assistance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him generously, but he sought only to keep himself safe and offered no real counsel.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以疾請告，至是，病甚辭位，章疏六上，乃許，除戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he requested leave on grounds of illness; by then his illness was severe and he resigned his post — six memorials in succession — and only then was he permitted, appointed minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took sick leave; his illness worsened and he resigned his councilorship — six memorials in all — before he was permitted to step down and was made minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年四十四，輟朝三日，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age forty-four; court was suspended for three days and he was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at forty-four; court mourning lasted three days and he was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，林甫生祥道，麟德初為右相，祥道即從一曾伯祖也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lin Fu fathered Xiangdao, who in early Longde was right chief minister — Xiangdao was Congyi's great-great-uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fu's son Xiangdao had been right chief minister in early Longde — he was Congyi's great-great-uncle.

sentences.zh: 令植從父兄齊賢，弘道初為侍中。

translations.literal: Lingzhi's paternal cousin Qixian was attendant-in-chief in early Hongdao.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi's cousin Qixian had been attendant-in-chief in early Hongdao.

sentences.zh: 自祥道至從一，劉氏凡三相。

translations.literal: From Xiangdao to Congyi, the Liu clan produced three chief ministers in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangdao to Congyi, the Liu family produced three chief ministers in all.

sentences.zh: 蕭復，字履初，太子太師嵩之孫，新昌公主之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu, courtesy name Luchu, was grandson of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Song and son of Princess Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu, courtesy name Luchu, was the grandson of Grand Preceptor Song and the son of Princess Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 父衡，太仆卿、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His father Heng was Minister of Imperial Studs and Commandant Escort of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heng had been Minister of Imperial Studs and commandant escort of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 少秉清操，其群從兄弟，競飾輿馬，以侈靡相尚，復衣浣濯之衣，獨居一室，習學不倦，非詞人儒士不與之遊。

translations.literal: From youth he held pure conduct; his cousins vied in decking out carriages and horses and prided themselves on extravagance, while Fu wore washed clothes, lived alone in one room, studied tirelessly, and associated only with literary men and Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated integrity; his cousins vied in lavish carriages and horses while he wore plain washed clothes, lived alone, studied tirelessly, and kept company only with scholars and literati.

sentences.zh: 伯華每嘆異之。

translations.literal: Bohua often sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Bohua often marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 以主廕，初為宮門郎，累至太子仆。

translations.literal: Through imperial consort privilege he first served as palace gate officer and rose in stages to Master of the Heir Apparent's Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Through imperial consort privilege he began as a palace gate officer and rose to Master of the Heir Apparent's Stud.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，連歲不稔，谷價翔貴，家貧，將鬻昭應別業。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era, successive years of poor harvest drove grain prices steeply up; his family was poor and he was about to sell his estate at Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangde, successive crop failures sent grain prices soaring; his family was poor and he was about to sell his estate at Zhaoying.

sentences.zh: 時宰相王縉聞其林泉之美，心欲之，乃使弟竑誘焉，曰：「足下之才，固宜居右職，如以別業奉家兄，當以要地處矣。

translations.literal: At the time chief minister Wang Jin heard of the beauty of its woods and springs and desired it; he had his younger brother Hong entice Fu, saying: "Your talent truly suits a high post — if you present the estate to my elder brother, you will be placed in an important position."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Wang Jin, hearing of its fine landscape, coveted it and sent his brother Hong to entice Fu: "Your talents deserve a high post — present the estate to my brother and you will receive an important appointment."

sentences.zh: 」復對曰：「仆以家貧而鬻舊業，將以拯濟孀幼耳，倘以易美職於身，令門內凍餒，非鄙夫之心也。

translations.literal: Fu replied: "I sell my old property because my family is poor, to rescue widows and children — if I traded it for a fine post for myself and let my household freeze and starve, that would not be this humble man's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied: "I am selling the estate because we are poor, to support widows and children — to trade it for a fine post while my household goes hungry is not in my nature."

sentences.zh: 」縉憾之，乃罷復官。

translations.literal: Jin resented this and dismissed Fu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took offense and had Fu dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 沈廢數年，復處之自若。

translations.literal: He lay in disuse for several years, yet Fu bore it with composure.
translations.idiomatic: He remained idle for years, yet Fu bore it with equanimity.

sentences.zh: 後累至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Later he rose in stages to director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose in stages to a director's post in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年，自常州刺史為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali he moved from prefect of Changzhou to prefect of Tanzhou and observer of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 14 he moved from prefect of Changzhou to prefect of Tanzhou and observer of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 及為同州刺史，州人阻饑，有京畿觀察使儲廩在境內，復輒以賑貸，為有司所劾，削階。

translations.literal: When he became prefect of Tongzhou the people were blocked by famine; there was a capital-region observer's granary within the prefecture, and Fu repeatedly used it for relief loans — he was impeached by the responsible offices and his rank step was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Tongzhou he found the people starving; a capital-region granary lay within his jurisdiction and he repeatedly drew on it for relief — the authorities impeached him and reduced his rank.

sentences.zh: 朋友唁之，復怡然曰：「茍利於人，敢憚薄罰。

translations.literal: Friends condoled with him; Fu said calmly: "If it benefits the people, how dare I shrink from a light punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: When friends condoled with him, Fu said calmly: "If it helped the people, I do not regret a light penalty."

sentences.zh: 」尋為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 建中末，普王為襄漢元帥，以復為戶部尚書、統軍長史，以復父名衡，特詔避之，未行。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong the Prince of Pu was commander of Xiang-Han; Fu was made minister of Revenue and army chief of staff — because Fu's father's name was Heng, a special edict ordered taboo avoidance, and he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianzhong the Prince of Pu was commander of Xiang-Han; Fu was appointed minister of Revenue and army chief of staff, but a special edict required him to avoid his father's name Heng, and he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 扈駕奉天，拜吏部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Escorting the emperor at Fengtian, he was appointed minister of Personnel and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the emperor at Fengtian, he was made minister of Personnel and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 復嘗奏曰：「宦者自艱難已來，初為監軍，自爾恩幸過重。

translations.literal: Fu once memorialized: "Since the time of hardship, eunuchs were first made army supervisors; from then their favor has been excessive."
translations.idiomatic: Fu once memorialized: "Since the crisis, eunuchs were first made army supervisors, and from then their favor has been excessive."

sentences.zh: 此輩只合委宮掖之寄，不可參兵機政事之權。

translations.literal: These men should only be entrusted with palace duties and must not participate in military affairs or governmental power.
translations.idiomatic: They should be confined to palace duties and must not share in military or governmental authority.

sentences.zh: 」上不悅，又請別對，奏云：「陛下臨禦之初，聖德光被，自用楊炎、盧杞秉政，惛瀆皇猷，以致今日。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; Fu again requested a separate audience and memorialized: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, sagely virtue shone abroad — since Yang Yan and Lu Qi were left to hold power, they have befouled the imperial design and brought us to today."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased; Fu requested a private audience and said: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, your virtue shone abroad — yet Yang Yan and Lu Qi were allowed to govern, befouling your design and bringing us to this pass."

sentences.zh: 今雖危急，伏願陛下深革睿思，微臣敢當此任。

translations.literal: Though the situation is now critical, I humbly beg Your Majesty to deeply reform your sagely thought — your humble servant dares undertake this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Though the crisis is grave, I beg Your Majesty to reform your thinking deeply — I dare undertake that charge.

sentences.zh: 若令臣依阿偷免，臣不敢曠職。

translations.literal: If you order me to fawn and evade, I dare not neglect my duty.
translations.idiomatic: If you expect me to fawn and evade responsibility, I cannot accept that.

sentences.zh: 」盧杞奏對於上前，阿諛順旨，復正色曰：「杞之詞不正。

translations.literal: Lu Qi answered before the throne with flattery to suit the emperor's wishes; Fu said sternly: "Qi's words are not upright."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi answered before the throne with flattery; Fu said sternly: "Qi's words are not upright."

sentences.zh: 」德宗愕然，退謂左右曰：「蕭復頗輕朕。

translations.literal: Dezong was startled and, on retiring, told his attendants: "Xiao Fu rather looks down on me."
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was startled and told his attendants afterward: "Xiao Fu rather looks down on me."

sentences.zh: 」遂令往江南宣撫。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to go to Jiangnan as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent him to Jiangnan as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先時，淮南節度陳少遊首稱臣於李希烈，鳳翔將李楚琳殺節度使張鎰以應硃泚，鎰判官韋臯先知隴州留後，首殺豳叛卒數百人，不應楚琳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huainan commissioner Chen Shaoyou was first to declare himself subject to Li Xilie; Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed commissioner Zhang Yi to respond to Zhu Ci; Yi's aide Wei Gao, knowing beforehand as acting Longzhou rear commander, was first to kill several hundred Bin mutineers and would not follow Chulin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huainan commissioner Chen Shaoyou was the first to submit to Li Xilie; Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed commissioner Zhang Yi to join Zhu Ci; Yi's aide Wei Gao, then acting rear commander at Longzhou, was first to execute several hundred Bin mutineers and refused to follow Chulin.

sentences.zh: 復江南使回，與宰相同對訖，復獨留，奏曰：「陛下自返宮闕，勛臣已蒙官爵，唯旌善懲惡，未有區分。

translations.literal: When Fu returned from his Jiangnan mission and, after answering together with the chief ministers, remained alone, he memorialized: "Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, meritorious subjects have received ranks and titles, but in honoring good and punishing evil there has been no distinction."
translations.idiomatic: When Fu returned from Jiangnan and, after the joint audience with the chief ministers, was kept behind, he said: "Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, the meritorious have been rewarded, but good and evil have not been clearly distinguished."

sentences.zh: 陳少遊將相之寄最崇，首敗臣節；

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou enjoyed the loftiest trust as general and minister, yet was first to break the subject's bond;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou enjoyed the highest trust as general and minister, yet was first to break his bond as a subject;

sentences.zh: 韋臯名宦最卑，特建忠義。

translations.literal: Wei Gao stood lowest among famous officials, yet specially established loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao stood lowest among notable officials, yet distinguished himself by loyalty.

sentences.zh: 請令韋臯代少遊，則天下明然知逆順之理。

translations.literal: I beg that Wei Gao be ordered to replace Shaoyou — then all under Heaven will clearly know the principle of rebellion and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Let Wei Gao replace Shaoyou, and all under Heaven will plainly see the difference between loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 」上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 復出，宰相李勉、盧翰、劉從一方同歸中書，中使馬欽緒至，揖從一，附耳語而退，諸相各歸閣。

translations.literal: Fu went out; chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi were returning together to the Secretariat when palace envoy Ma Qinxu arrived, bowed to Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew — each minister returned to his office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu left; chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi were returning to the Secretariat when palace envoy Ma Qinxu bowed to Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew — each minister returned to his office.

sentences.zh: 從一詣復曰：「適欽緒宣旨，令與公商量朝來所奏便進，勿令李勉、盧翰知。

translations.literal: Congyi went to Fu and said: "Just now Qinxu announced the decree: discuss with you the morning's memorial and submit it promptly — do not let Li Mian or Lu Han know."
translations.idiomatic: Congyi went to Fu and said: "Qinxu has just conveyed the decree: discuss this morning's memorial with you and submit it at once — do not let Li Mian or Lu Han know."

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「適來奏對，亦聞斯旨，然未諭聖心，已面陳述，上意尚爾，復未敢言其事。

translations.literal: Fu said: "In the audience just now I also heard this intent, but I had not yet grasped the sacred mind; I already stated it face to face, and the emperor's mind is still thus — I did not yet dare speak of the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "I heard that intent in the audience just now, but the emperor's mind was not yet clear; I stated my view to his face, and his mind is still unsettled — I did not yet dare press the matter."

sentences.zh: 」復又曰：「唐、虞有僉曰之論，朝廷有事，尚合與公卿同議。

translations.literal: Fu added: "Tang and Yu had the doctrine of collective assent — when the court has business, it should still be deliberated with the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Fu added: "Even Tang and Yu deliberated collectively — when the court has business, it should still be discussed with the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 今勉、翰不可在相位，即去之；

translations.literal: If Mian and Han should not hold chief-minister posts, remove them;
translations.idiomatic: If Mian and Han should not hold chief-minister posts, remove them;

sentences.zh: 既在相位，合同商量，何故獨避此之一節？

translations.literal: if they remain in those posts, they ought to deliberate together — why single out this one matter to exclude them?
translations.idiomatic: if they remain in office, they ought to deliberate together — why exclude them from this one matter alone?

sentences.zh: 且與公行之無爽，但恐浸以成俗，此政之大弊也。

translations.literal: Going along with you on this occasion would not be wrong, but I fear it will gradually become custom — that is a great defect in government.
translations.idiomatic: I could go along with you this once, but I fear it will become habit — that is a grave defect in government.

sentences.zh: 」竟不言於從一。

translations.literal: In the end he did not speak of it to Congyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not comply with Congyi.

sentences.zh: 從一奏之，上浸不悅。

translations.literal: Congyi reported this; the emperor grew increasingly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi reported this, and the emperor grew increasingly displeased.

sentences.zh: 復累表辭疾，請罷知政事，從之，守太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Fu repeatedly memorialized illness and asked to resign from managing state affairs; the request was granted and he was retained as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu repeatedly memorialized illness and asked to leave the council; the request was granted and he was retained as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐郜國公主親累，檢校左庶子，於饒州安置。

translations.literal: In the third year, implicated through kinship with Princess Guo, he was made acting Left Mentor and settled at Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, implicated through kinship with Princess Guo, he was made acting Left Mentor and posted to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，終於饒州，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at Raozhou at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at Raozhou at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 復門望高華，誌礪名節，與流俗不甚通狎。

translations.literal: Fu's family standing was lofty and splendid; he aspired to integrity and did not mingle much with the vulgar world.
translations.idiomatic: Fu came from an eminent house, aspired to integrity, and kept aloof from vulgar company.

sentences.zh: 及登臺輔，臨事不茍，頗為同列所嫉，以故居位不久。

translations.literal: When he reached the council dais he was unbending in affairs and was much resented by colleagues, so his tenure was brief.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the council he was unbending in office and was much resented by colleagues, so his tenure was brief.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，居家甚睦，為族子所累，晏然屏退，口未嘗言。

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, his household was very harmonious; when implicated by a clansman's offense he withdrew calmly and never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and friendly by nature, he kept a harmonious household; when implicated by a clansman's offense he withdrew quietly and never spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 郜國公主者，肅宗之女也，出降駙馬蕭升，升於復為從兄弟，升早卒。

translations.literal: Princess Guo was a daughter of Suzong; she married the imperial son-in-law Xiao Sheng — Sheng was Fu's cousin, and Sheng died early.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guo was a daughter of Emperor Suzong; she married the imperial son-in-law Xiao Sheng, Fu's cousin, who died young.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，蜀州別駕蕭鼎、商州豐陽令韋恪、前彭州司馬李萬、太子詹事李升等出入主第，穢聲流聞。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan, Shuozhou vice-prefect Xiao Ding, Fengyang magistrate of Shangzhou Wei Ke, former Pengzhou military adjutant Li Wan, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Sheng, and others came and went at the princess's residence — scandalous reports spread.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan, Xiao Ding, vice-prefect of Shuozhou, Wei Ke, magistrate of Fengyang in Shangzhou, former Pengzhou adjutant Li Wan, Grand Mentor Li Sheng, and others frequented the princess's residence, and scandalous rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，幽主於別第，李萬決殺，升貶嶺南，蕭鼎、韋恪決四十，長流嶺表。

translations.literal: Dezong was enraged, confined the princess in a separate residence, ordered Li Wan executed by decapitation, banished Sheng to Lingnan, and sentenced Xiao Ding and Wei Ke to forty blows and long exile beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was enraged, confined the princess in a separate residence, had Li Wan executed, banished Sheng to Lingnan, and sentenced Xiao Ding and Wei Ke to forty blows and exile beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 又言公主行厭禱，其子位為禱文，位弟佩、儒、偲及異父兄駙馬都尉裴液，並長流端州。

translations.literal: It was also said the princess practiced curse-prayer; her son Wei drafted the prayer text; Wei's younger brothers Pei, Ru, and Si and her half-brother Commandant Escort Pei Ye were all long-exiled to Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It was also said the princess practiced curse-prayer; her son Wei drafted the text; Wei's brothers Pei, Ru, and Si and her half-brother Commandant Escort Pei Ye were all exiled to Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 公主女為皇太子妃，即順宗也。

translations.literal: The princess's daughter was consort to the Crown Prince — that is, Shunzong.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's daughter was consort to the crown prince — the future Emperor Shunzong.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，亦請與妃離婚。

translations.literal: The crown prince, in fear, also requested divorce from his consort.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in fear, also asked to divorce his consort.

sentences.zh: 六年，郜國薨，位兄弟及液詔還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Princess Guo died; Wei and his brothers and Ye were ordered back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Princess Guo died; Wei, his brothers, and Ye were ordered back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 液父徽，初尚郜國；

translations.literal: Ye's father Hui had first married Princess Guo;
translations.idiomatic: Ye's father Hui had first married Princess Guo;

sentences.zh: 徽卒，降蕭升。

translations.literal: when Hui died she married Xiao Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: after Hui died she married Xiao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 柳渾，字夷曠，襄州人，其先自河東徙焉。

translations.literal: Liu Hun, courtesy name Yikuang, was a native of Xiangzhou; his ancestors had moved there from Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun, courtesy name Yikuang, was from Xiangzhou; his family had moved there from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 六代祖惔，梁僕射。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Tan was a Liang dynasty vice director.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Tan had been a vice director under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 渾少孤，父慶休，官至渤海丞，而誌學棲貧。

translations.literal: Hun was orphaned young; his father Qingxiu reached the post of Bohai assistant magistrate, yet aspired to learning and lived in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Hun lost his father young; his father Qingxiu had risen to assistant magistrate of Bohai, yet Hun aspired to learning and lived in poverty.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，舉進士，補單父尉。

translations.literal: In early Tianbao he passed the jinshi and was made magistrate of Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 至德中，為江西采訪使皇甫侁判官，累除衢州司馬。

translations.literal: In Zhide he served as administrative aide to Jiangxi investigation commissioner Huangfu Shen and was promoted in stages to military adjutant of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide he served as chief clerk to Jiangxi investigation commissioner Huangfu Shen and was promoted in stages to military adjutant of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up that post he was summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 臺中執法之地，動限儀矩，渾性放，不甚檢束，僚長拘局，忿其疏縱。

translations.literal: The censorate is a place of law enforcement where deportment is strictly regulated; Hun's nature was free and he did not much restrain himself — senior colleagues, confined by rules, resented his laxness.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate enforces the law and demands strict deportment; Hun was by nature unrestrained, and his superiors, bound by protocol, resented his laxness.

sentences.zh: 渾不樂，乞外任，執政惜其才，奏為左補闕。

translations.literal: Hun was unhappy and requested an outside post; the chief ministers valued his talent and memorialized to make him Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy there, Hun asked for an outside post; the chief ministers valued his talent and had him made Left Remonstrator instead.

sentences.zh: 明年，除殿中侍御史，知江西租庸院事。

translations.literal: The next year he was made palace attending censor and placed in charge of Jiangxi rent-and-corvée affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made palace attending censor in charge of Jiangxi rent-and-corvée affairs.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，魏少遊鎮江西，奏署判官，累授檢校司封郎中。

translations.literal: In early Dali, when Wei Shaoyou governed Jiangxi, he memorialized to appoint Hun administrative aide and promoted him in stages to acting director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In early Dali, when Wei Shaoyou governed Jiangxi, he brought Hun on as chief clerk and promoted him in stages to acting director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 州理有開元寺僧與徒夜飲，醉而延火，歸罪於守門瘖奴，軍候亦受財，同上其狀，少遊信焉。

translations.literal: In the prefectural capital, monks of Kaiyuan Temple drank at night with disciples, became drunk and spread fire, then blamed the mute gatekeeping slave; the military patrol also took bribes and jointly submitted the report — Shaoyou believed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectural seat, monks of Kaiyuan Temple drank with disciples at night, became drunk, and set a fire, then blamed the mute gatekeeper; the military patrol also took bribes and filed a joint report — Shaoyou believed it.

sentences.zh: 人知奴冤，莫肯言。

translations.literal: People knew the slave was wronged but none would speak.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew the slave was innocent, but no one would speak up.

sentences.zh: 渾與崔祐甫遽入白，少遊驚問，醉僧首伏。

translations.literal: Hun and Cui Youfu hurried in to report; Shaoyou asked in alarm, and the drunken monk confessed first.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and Cui Youfu hurried in to report; Shaoyou was startled, and the drunken monk confessed at once.

sentences.zh: 既而謝曰：「微二君子，幾成老夫暗劣矣。

translations.literal: He then apologized: "But for you two gentlemen, I would nearly have become an old man's blunder."
translations.idiomatic: He then apologized: "But for you two gentlemen, I would nearly have made a fool of myself."

sentences.zh: 」自此以公正聞。

translations.literal: From then he was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 及路嗣恭領鎮，復以為都團練副使。

translations.literal: When Lu Sigong took command of the circuit, Hun was again made deputy overall training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Sigong took command of the circuit, Hun was again made deputy overall training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜袁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 居二年，崔祐甫入相，薦為諫議大夫、浙江東西黜陟使，累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: After two years Cui Youfu entered the council and recommended him as remonstrance grandee and promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Zhejiang East and West; he rose in stages to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After two years Cui Youfu became chief minister and recommended him as remonstrance grandee and promotion-and-demotion commissioner for eastern and western Zhejiang; he rose in stages to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及駕在奉天，微服徒行，遁終南山谷，逾旬方達行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial train was at Fengtian, he went in plain clothes on foot, fled into the Zhongnan mountain valleys, and only after more than ten days reached the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was at Fengtian, he went in plain clothes on foot, fled into the Zhongnan mountains, and reached the traveling court only after more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 扈從至梁州，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Escorting the emperor to Liangzhou, he was changed to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the emperor to Liangzhou, he was made Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，渾之歸行在，賊泚籍其名甚，願以致之，猶疑匿在閭裏，乃加宰相。

translations.literal: At first, when Hun returned to the traveling court, the rebel Zhu Ci greatly desired his name and wished to win him over, still suspecting he was hidden among the people — therefore he was additionally made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun first reached the traveling court, the rebel Zhu Ci coveted him and still suspected he was hiding among the people — so the court made him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及克復，渾尚名載，乃上言：「頃為狂賊點穢，臣實恥稱舊名，矧字或帶戈，時當偃武，請改名渾。」

translations.literal: After recovery, Hun's name was still on the rebel rolls; he memorialized: "Recently the mad rebel defiled my name — your servant is truly ashamed to bear the old name; moreover the character may carry the 'spear' radical, and the time calls for laying down arms — I beg to change my name to Hun."
translations.idiomatic: After the recovery, Hun's name still appeared on the rebel rolls; he memorialized: "The rebel recently defiled my name, and I am ashamed to bear it; moreover the character contains the 'spear' radical, and this is a time to lay down arms — I beg to change my name to Hun."

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，拜兵部侍郎，封宜城縣伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was appointed vice minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Yicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 he was made vice minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，加同平章事，仍判門下省。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was additionally made Associate Grand Councilor and continued to oversee the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he was additionally made Associate Grand Councilor while continuing to oversee the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時上命玉工為帶，墜壞一銙，乃私市以補；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor ordered a jade artisan to make a belt; one link fell and broke, and he privately bought a replacement to mend it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered a jade artisan to make a belt; one link broke off, and the artisan secretly bought a replacement;

sentences.zh: 及獻，上指曰：「此何不相類？

translations.literal: when he presented it the emperor pointed and said: "Why does this not match?"
translations.idiomatic: when he presented it the emperor pointed and said: "Why does this not match?"

sentences.zh: 」工人伏罪，上命決死。

translations.literal: The artisan confessed guilt and the emperor ordered immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: The artisan confessed, and the emperor ordered him executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 詔至中書，渾執曰：「陛下若便殺則已，若下有司，即須議讞。

translations.literal: When the edict reached the Secretariat, Hun held it and said: "If Your Majesty kills at once, so be it; if it goes to the responsible offices, there must be deliberation on the sentence."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached the Secretariat, Hun held it back and said: "If Your Majesty kills him at once, so be it; but if the case goes to the offices, the sentence must be deliberated."

sentences.zh: 且方春行刑，容臣條奏定罪。

translations.literal: Moreover, it is spring — a season for executions — allow your servant to memorialize item by item to fix the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it is spring, when executions are traditionally restrained — allow me to memorialize on the proper sentence.

sentences.zh: 」以誤傷乘輿器服，杖六十，余工釋放，詔從之。

translations.literal: For mistakenly damaging imperial carriage regalia he was sentenced to sixty blows; the other artisans were released — the edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: For mistakenly damaging imperial regalia the artisan was sentenced to sixty blows; the others were released, and the edict followed Hun's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 復奏：「故尚書左丞田季羔，公忠正直，先朝名臣。

translations.literal: Hun again memorialized: "The late Left Vice Director Tian Jigao was loyal, upright, and a famous minister of the previous reign."
translations.idiomatic: Hun memorialized again: "The late Left Vice Director Tian Jigao was loyal, upright, and a renowned minister of the previous reign."

sentences.zh: 其祖、父皆以孝行旌表門閭，京城隋朝舊第，季羔一家而已。

translations.literal: His grandfather and father were both honored at their gate for filial conduct; of the old Sui-dynasty mansions in the capital, only Jigao's household remains.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather and father were both honored at their gate for filial piety; of the old Sui mansions in the capital, only Jigao's household remains.

sentences.zh: 今被堂侄伯強進狀，請貨宅召市人馬，以討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Now his cousin's son Boqiang has submitted a petition asking to mortgage the house and hire marketplace men and horses to campaign against the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Now his cousin's son Boqiang has petitioned to mortgage the house and hire marketplace men and horses for a campaign against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 一開此門，恐滋不逞。

translations.literal: Once this door is opened, I fear it will breed the unruly.
translations.idiomatic: Once this door is opened, I fear it will encourage opportunists.

sentences.zh: 討賊自有國計，豈資僥幸之徒？

translations.literal: Suppressing rebels has its own state plans — how can we rely on adventurers?
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing rebels is a matter of state policy — how can we rely on adventurers?

sentences.zh: 且毀棄義門，虧損風教，望少責罰，亦可懲勸。

translations.literal: Moreover it would destroy a house of righteousness and damage moral teaching — I hope for a light punishment that may also serve as warning and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it would destroy a house honored for righteousness and damage public morals — I hope for a light punishment that may also serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 」上可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 先時，韓滉自浙西入覲，朝廷委政待之，至於調兵食，籠鹽鐵，勾官吏贓罰，鋤豪強兼並，上悉仗焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Huang came from Zhexi to audience; the court entrusted him with government, even in deploying troops and grain, monopolizing salt and iron, investigating officials' graft and fines, and uprooting powerful families' encroachments — the emperor relied on him entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Han Huang came from Zhexi to court; the government entrusted him with wide powers — troop and grain deployments, salt and iron monopolies, graft investigations, and breaking up powerful encroachments — and the emperor relied on him entirely.

sentences.zh: 每奏事，或日旰，他相充位而已，公卿救過不能暇，無敢枝梧者。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported, audiences sometimes lasted until sundown; other chief ministers merely filled their seats, the high officials had no leisure beyond covering their faults, and none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: His audiences sometimes lasted until sundown; other chief ministers merely held their seats, officials scrambled to cover their faults, and none dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 渾雖滉所引，心惡其專政，正色讓之曰：「先相公以狷察為相，不滿歲而罷；

translations.literal: Though Hun had been introduced by Huang, he detested Huang's monopoly of power and said sternly: "The former chief minister was dismissed within a year for being harsh and suspicious as chief minister;"
translations.idiomatic: Though Hun owed his rise to Huang, he detested Huang's monopoly of power and said sternly: "Your predecessor was dismissed within a year for being harsh and suspicious in office;"

sentences.zh: 今相公搒吏於省中至死，且非刑人之地，奈何蹈前非而又甚焉？

translations.literal: "now you beat a clerk to death in the ministry — and that is not a place for punishment — why repeat the earlier fault and go even further?"
translations.idiomatic: "now you beat a clerk to death in the ministry — which is not a place for executions — why repeat that error and go even further?"

sentences.zh: 專立威福，豈尊主卑臣之禮！

translations.literal: "To monopolize authority and favor — is that the ritual of honoring the ruler and lowering the minister!"
translations.idiomatic: "To monopolize power and favor — is that how a minister honors his ruler!"

sentences.zh: 」滉感悟愧悔，為霽威焉。

translations.literal: Huang was moved to awareness and shame and moderated his severity.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was moved to shame and moderated his severity.

sentences.zh: 及白誌貞除浙西觀察使，渾奏曰：「誌貞一末吏憸人，縱稱廉謹，不當頓居重職。

translations.literal: When Bai Zhizhen was appointed observer of Zhexi, Hun memorialized: "Zhizhen is a petty clerk and treacherous man — even if called honest and cautious, he should not suddenly hold a weighty post."
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zhizhen was appointed observer of Zhexi, Hun memorialized: "Zhizhen is a petty, treacherous clerk — even if called honest, he should not suddenly hold a weighty post."

sentences.zh: 」適遇渾以疾稱告，即日詔下。

translations.literal: It happened that Hun reported illness that same day, and the edict was issued at once.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hun reported illness, and the edict was issued at once.

sentences.zh: 疾間，因乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Between bouts of illness he asked to retire on grounds of old bones, but a gracious edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: During his illness he asked to retire, but a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 其判門下，主吏白當過官，渾愀然曰：「列官分職，復更撓之，非禮法也。

translations.literal: While overseeing the Chancellery, the chief clerk reported that he should call on officials; Hun said gravely: "Each office has its division of duty — to interfere again is not ritual law."
translations.idiomatic: While overseeing the Chancellery, the chief clerk said he should call on officials; Hun said gravely: "Each office has its duties — to interfere again is not proper procedure."

sentences.zh: 千里辭家，以幹微祿，邑主辭辦，豈慮無能，矧旌善進賢，事不在此。

translations.literal: "Men leave home a thousand li to seek a modest salary — the local lord declines to receive them, yet need we fear they are incapable? Moreover, honoring good and advancing the worthy is not this business."
translations.idiomatic: "Men travel a thousand li from home for a modest salary — hosts decline to receive them, yet need we fear they are incapable? Honoring virtue and advancing talent is not done this way."

sentences.zh: 」故其年註擬，無退量者。

translations.literal: Therefore in that year's appointments there were none who withdrew in modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in that year's appointments none declined out of false modesty.

sentences.zh: 及渾瑊與吐蕃會盟之日，上御便殿謂宰相曰：「和戎息師，國之大計，今日將士與卿同歡。

translations.literal: On the day Hun Zhen allied with the Tibetans, the emperor attended the side hall and told the chief ministers: "Making peace with the barbarians and resting the armies is the great plan of state — today soldiers and ministers rejoice together."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Hun Zhen's alliance with Tibet, the emperor met the chief ministers in the side hall and said: "Peace with the frontier and resting the armies is the great plan of state — today soldiers and ministers rejoice together."

sentences.zh: 」馬燧前賀曰：今之一盟，百年內更無蕃寇。

translations.literal: Ma Sui stepped forward to congratulate him: "With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui stepped forward to congratulate him: "With this alliance, Tibet will not raid us again for a hundred years."

sentences.zh: 」渾曰：「五帝無誥誓之盟，皆在季末。
