translations.literal: Hun said: "The Five Emperors had no alliances of command and oath — those all came at the end of an age."
translations.idiomatic: Hun said: "The Five Emperors made no sworn alliances — those belong only to the end of an age."

sentences.zh: 今盛明之代，豈又行於夷狄！

translations.literal: In this flourishing and enlightened era, how can it be practiced toward the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: In this flourishing age, how can we practice it toward barbarians!

sentences.zh: 人面獸心，難以信結，今日盟約，臣竊憂之。

translations.literal: Human faces with beast hearts — hard to bind by trust; today's treaty, your servant privately fears it.
translations.idiomatic: They have human faces but beast hearts and cannot be trusted; I privately fear today's treaty.

sentences.zh: 」李晟繼言曰：「臣生長邊城，知蕃戎心，今日之事，誠如渾言。

translations.literal: Li Sheng followed, saying: "Your servant grew up on the frontier and knows the Tibetan mind — today's affair is truly as Hun says."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng added: "I grew up on the frontier and know the Tibetan mind — today's affair is exactly as Hun says."

sentences.zh: 」上變色曰：「柳渾書生，未達邊事；

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "Liu Hun is a bookish man who does not understand frontier affairs;"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened: "Liu Hun is a scholar who does not understand frontier affairs;"

sentences.zh: 大臣智略，果亦有斯言乎！

translations.literal: "can a great minister's wisdom and strategy truly also speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: "can a great minister's wisdom truly speak thus!"

sentences.zh: 」皆頓首俯伏，遽令歸中書。

translations.literal: All knocked their heads and lay prostrate, and he quickly ordered them back to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: All prostrated themselves, and he quickly sent them back to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其夜三更，邠寧節度韓遊瑰飛驛叩苑門，奏盟會不成，將校覆沒，兵臨近鎮，上驚嘆，即遞其表以示渾。

translations.literal: That night at the third watch, Binning commissioner Han Yougui sent a flying relay to knock at the park gate, reporting the alliance had failed, officers wiped out, and troops pressing a nearby command — the emperor exclaimed in alarm and at once forwarded the memorial to show Hun.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch, Binning commissioner Han Yougui sent an urgent relay knocking at the park gate: the alliance had failed, officers were wiped out, and enemy troops pressed a nearby command. The emperor exclaimed in alarm and at once showed the memorial to Hun.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，臨軒慰勉渾曰：「卿文儒之士，而萬里知軍戎之情。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he faced the hall and comforted Hun: "You are a literary and Confucian man, yet a thousand li away you knew the mood of the armies."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he faced the hall and comforted Hun: "You are a scholar, yet from afar you knew the armies' mind."

sentences.zh: 」自此驟加禮異。

translations.literal: From then he suddenly added exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he treated Hun with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 時張延賞與渾同列，延賞怙權矜己，而嫉渾守正，俾其所厚謂渾曰：「相公舊德，但節言於廟堂，則重位可久。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yanshang sat in the same rank as Hun; Yanshang relied on power and prided himself, yet resented Hun's uprightness, and had a favorite tell Hun: "The chief minister's old virtue — if you only moderate your words in the hall, the high post can last long."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang then shared rank with Hun; Yanshang was arrogant in power and resented Hun's integrity, and had an ally tell him: "With your long-standing virtue, if you only moderate your words in court, your high post can endure."
Thus he concluded.

sentences.zh: 渾曰：「為吾謝張相公，柳渾頭可斷，而舌不可禁也。

translations.literal: Hun said: "Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang — Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced."
translations.idiomatic: Hun said: "Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang — Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced."

sentences.zh: 」自是為其所擠，尋除常侍，罷知政事。

translations.literal: From then he was squeezed out by Yanshang; soon he was made Regular Attendant and dismissed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then Yanshang squeezed him out; soon he was made Regular Attendant and removed from the council.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年二月，以疾終，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhenyuan 5 he died of illness at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 渾母兄識，，篤意文章，有重名於開元、天寶間，與蕭穎士、元德秀、劉迅相亞。

translations.literal: Hun's elder brother by the same mother, Shi, devoted himself to literature and had a great name between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's elder brother Shi devoted himself to literature and was renowned in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 其練理創端往往詣極，當時作者，鹹伏其簡拔，而趣尚辨博。

translations.literal: His refinement in structure and openings often reached the utmost; writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, while his bent favored disputation and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: His structural refinement and openings often reached the highest level; contemporary writers all acknowledged his concise mastery, though his taste favored disputation and breadth.

sentences.zh: 渾亦善為文，然趨時向功，非沈思之所及。

translations.literal: Hun also wrote well, yet he aimed at the times and sought achievement — not what deep reflection could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Hun also wrote well, but he aimed at timely success rather than the depth of contemplative writing.

sentences.zh: 渾警辯，好諧謔放達，與人交，豁然無隱。

translations.literal: Hun was quick and eloquent, fond of wit, jest, and free openness; in dealing with people he was candid and hid nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was quick-witted and eloquent, fond of humor and easy openness; in company he was candid and hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 性節儉，不治產業，官至丞相，假宅而居。

translations.literal: By nature frugal, he did not manage estates; though he reached chief minister, he lived in a borrowed house.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he did not build an estate; though he rose to chief minister, he lived in a borrowed house.

sentences.zh: 罷相數日，則命親族尋勝，宴醉方歸，陶陶然忘其黜免。

translations.literal: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, return only when drunk from feasting, and forget his dismissal in high spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of leaving office he would take kin to scenic outings, return drunk from feasting, and cheerfully forget his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 時李勉、盧翰皆退罷居第，相謂曰：「吾輩方柳宜城，悉為拘俗之人也。」

translations.literal: At the time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired to their residences and said to each other: "Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian and Lu Han, both retired at home, said to each other: "Beside Liu of Yicheng, we are all prisoners of convention."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：張鎰、蕭復、柳渾，節行才能訏謨亮直，皆足相明主，平泰階，而盧杞忌之於前，延賞排之於後，管仲有言：「任君子，使小人間之，害霸也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun — in integrity, ability, remonstrance, and bright uprightness — were all sufficient to assist a enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi resented them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: "Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between — that harms hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun — upright in conduct, capable in office, frank in counsel — were all fit to serve an enlightened ruler and restore order; yet Lu Qi resented them early and Yanshang drove them out later. Guan Zhong said: "Employ gentlemen and let petty men come between — that ruins hegemony."

sentences.zh: 」德宗黜賢相，位奸臣，致硃泚、懷光之亂，是失其人也，豈尤其時哉！

translations.literal: Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ones, bringing on the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang — this was losing the right men; how can one blame only the times!
translations.idiomatic: Dezong dismissed worthy ministers and elevated traitors, bringing on the rebellions of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang — he lost the right men; how can one blame the times alone!

sentences.zh: 河清歿於王事，乃顯忠貞；

translations.literal: Heqing died in the king's service and thereby showed loyalty and constancy;
translations.idiomatic: Heqing died in the state's service and thereby proved his loyalty;

sentences.zh: 從一舉自奸人，固宜循默。

translations.literal: Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly should have kept silent and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was promoted by traitors and could only have kept silent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：得人則興，失人則亡。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Gain the right men and the state flourishes; lose them and it perishes.

sentences.zh: 鎰、復、渾去，宗社其殃。

translations.literal: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi, Fu, and Hun were driven away, the dynasty suffered for it.
